column1: # Space Stranding order board.
# Tab-separated, one row per order. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what
# the facilities want moved. Parsed once at load by scripts/orders/order_book.gd
# and never written to at runtime - accepted, delivered and abandoned live in
# the save, keyed by code. The moment this file is written by the running game
# it stops being something you can edit.
#   tools/tsv-editor.ps1
# THE CODE
# code      100-999, opaque, sequential, NEVER REUSED. It is diegetic - it goes
#           on the crate, on the receipt, and in anything a character says - so
#           one number refers to one object everywhere. Do NOT encode the origin
#           in the first digit: moving a facility would renumber the world.
# ROUTING
# origin    facility id the order is offered at, or the literal `world` for
#           cargo that is already lying out there. A `world` row is authored in
#           the scene - drag a crate in, set its code - and this row supplies
#           everything else about it.
# destination
#           facility id the cargo is wanted at. The pad there is the only one
#           that will accept it.
# requires  a code that must be delivered before this one is offered. Blank for
#           none. One step only; there is no dependency graph.
# THE CARGO
# type      materials  raw stock. Buildable with, once construction exists.
#           upgrade    a package that installs on the rover or the suit.
#           sample     science payload. Usually the fragile ones.
#           personal   somebody's belongings. Worth little, means a lot.
#           Contents only. Whether the player may USE a crate is `owner`, which
#           is runtime state and not in this file - order cargo is owned by its
#           order until it is delivered. See docs/02-Systems/Orders.md.
# crates    how many boxes spawn on the origin's dock. The rover holds six, so
#           anything above six is deliberately a two-trip order.
# mass_kg   per crate. SETS the crate's mass - it is not a second copy of a
#           number that also lives in the inspector.
# fragility per crate, 0-4. Multiplies every bit of damage taken. 0.2 is pipe
#           stock, 2.4 is instruments. Sets crate.fragility.
# value     per crate, pristine. Sets crate.value, and the pad pays
#           value * condition^1.5 - so a half-condition crate pays 35%, not 50.
# deadline_s
#           PARKED. Always 0. Timed orders were designed and deliberately not
#           built: a clock says the opposite of what payout = condition^1.5
#           says, and the flare interaction has to be solved before one can
#           exist. The column is here because the TSV editor cannot add
#           columns, and hand-surgery on this file later is worse than a column
#           of zeroes now. See docs/07-Decisions/Decision-Log.md, 2026-08-31.
# FLAVOUR
# title     what the board calls it.
# issuer    whose voice the terminal speaks in. Blank for an unattended board.
# blurb     one line. The terminal shows it under the title.
code

Ice cores from the deep shadow. They have never been above freezing and would rather stay that way.
